The day planner discussed a reminder about lounge layout after a late message. Incident report for routine companion animal desk handling at Aurelia Skyways.

I opened the shift with the usual desk check and reviewed the live service board, the kennel handoff notes, and the carrier positions on the floor. The lounge layout had been adjusted earlier in the day to keep the passage clear for the ground team, and I confirmed that the lanes for pets in transit were still open and easy to monitor. During the first round of traveler contact, a minor service change came through for one booking, and the desk ledger was updated right away to match the revised handling plan. The carrier was moved carefully by the ground team between services, with the label facing up and the seal left intact. No distress was reported from the pet, and the traveler was kept informed in plain terms.

A later check found a brief delay in the return of one holding cart, which meant the loading area needed a quick reset before the next handover. I asked the staff member at the counter to pause the next intake, and I confirmed that the carrier for the affected pet remained secured and away from foot traffic. The desk then logged the change in sequence, noted the condition of the carrier, and recorded that the pet remained calm. Sara Khan and Samuel Rossi were both advised that the desk was managing the flow and that there was no welfare issue. The background work stayed routine, with the ground team continuing careful movement and the staff keeping the ledger current.

I closed the matter by checking the lounge layout again, clearing the path near the service rail, and confirming that the transfer notes matched the physical placement of the carriers. The follow-up was to keep the updated arrangement in place for the rest of the shift and to pass the note to the next coordinator so the same layout and handling pattern could be maintained. No further disruption came through, and all records were left in order. Companion Animal Travel Desk
